title: for since ago
subtitle: for three days / since Monday / three days ago
summary: Use for with a period of time, since with the start of a period, and ago to say how long before now something happened.

lesson.heading: for and since
lesson.text: We use **for** and **since** to say *how long*. Jane is in Ireland now. She arrived on Monday, so today is her third day there. We can say it in two ways.

examples.text: Jane is in Ireland. She **has been** there **for three days**.
Jane is in Ireland. She **has been** there **since Monday**.

lesson.heading: What comes after for and after since
columns: since + the start of the period
lesson.note: **for** = how long the period is. **since** = when the period started.

left.label: for + a period of time
examples: Richard has been in Canada **for six months**. (not ~~since six months~~)
We've been waiting **for two hours**. (not ~~since two hours~~)
I've lived in London **for a long time**.

right.label: since + the start of the period
examples: Richard has been in Canada **since January**. (= from January to now)
We've been waiting **since 9 o'clock**. (= from 9 o'clock to now)
I've lived in London **since I was ten years old**.

lesson.heading: ago
lesson.text: **ago** = before now. We use **ago** with the past (**started / did / had / was** etc.). The time word comes first, then **ago**.

examples.text: Susan started her new job **three weeks ago**.
*A:* When did Tom go out? *B:* **Ten minutes ago**.
Life was very different **a hundred years ago**.

left.label: ago + past
examples: Lynn and Mark **got** married **20 years ago**.

right.label: for + present perfect
right.text: We say how long a situation has continued.
examples: She **has been** in Ireland **for three days**.
Lynn and Mark **have been** married **for 20 years**.

lesson.text: Quick test: if the words answer *when?* (Monday, 1985, Christmas), use **since**. If they answer *how long?* (three days, six months), use **for**.

exercises.prompt: Jane has been in Ireland ___ Monday.
exercises.explanation: Monday is the start of the period, so we use since.

exercises.prompt: My aunt has lived in Australia ___ 15 years.
exercises.explanation: 15 years is a period of time, so we use for.

exercises.prompt: Jennifer is in her office. She has been there ___ 7 o'clock.
exercises.explanation: 7 o'clock is the start of the period, so we use since.

exercises.prompt: The bus is late. We've been waiting ___ 20 minutes.
exercises.explanation: 20 minutes is a period of time: for 20 minutes.

exercises.prompt: India has been an independent country ___ 1947.
exercises.explanation: 1947 is the start of the period, so we use since.

exercises.prompt: Michael has been in hospital ___ October.
exercises.explanation: October is when the period started: since October.

exercises.prompt: Does each time expression come after for or after since?
Lynn and Mark have been married ___.
exercises.explanation: have been + for + a period of time: for 20 years.
got is the past, so we use ago: 20 years ago.

exercises.prompt: I first met Sue in 2002. I've known her ___.
exercises.explanation: 2002 is the start of the period: I've known her since 2002.

exercises.prompt: Jack is here. He arrived on Tuesday. Say how long he has been here.
exercises.answer: Jack has been here since Tuesday.
exercises.explanation: Tuesday is the start of the period, so we use since.

exercises.statement: Richard has been in Canada since six months.
exercises.explanation: Richard has been in Canada for six months. six months is a period of time, so we use for.
